walkthroughs.body_html: Brown overturned Plessy in 1954; Eisenhower deployed the 101st Airborne in 1957 to enforce desegregation at Little Rock. The Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-56) launched MLK as a national leader. Greensboro sit-ins in February 1960 spread to 50 cities. Freedom Rides in 1961 challenged interstate segregation. Birmingham 1963, with fire hoses and dogs televised, mobilised national opinion.

Kennedy proposed civil rights legislation in June 1963 after Birmingham. The March on Washington in August 1963 and his November assassination created momentum. Johnson's Senate skills and southern background drove the Civil Rights Act through in July 1964. Selma marches in March 1965 and 'Bloody Sunday' on 7 March prompted the Voting Rights Act, signed on 6 August 1965.

Traditional 'top-down' accounts emphasise MLK and presidential leadership. Bottom-up histories such as Charles Payne's I've Got the Light of Freedom (1995) stress grassroots organising by SNCC and local leaders like Ella Baker and Fannie Lou Hamer. The 1965 Voting Rights Act dramatically raised Black registration; in Mississippi from 6 per cent in 1964 to 60 per cent by 1968.

mcqs.q: What did Brown v Board of Education decide in 1954?
options: Brown v Board of Education immediately desegregated all schools in America.
The Supreme Court ruled that 'separate but equal' schools were inherently unequal, overturning Plessy v Ferguson and beginning legal dismantling of school segregation.
Brown v Board ended slavery in the southern states.
Malcolm X and MLK were close allies who jointly led the March on Washington.

mcqs.q: How did Malcolm X's approach differ from MLK's?
options: Malcolm X and MLK were close allies who jointly led the March on Washington.
MLK preached nonviolent integration; Malcolm X (until 1964) advocated black self-defence, separatism, and rejected integration as a goal — though both shifted positions over time.
Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
Malcolm X advocated violent terrorism against white Americans.

mcqs.q: How was the US civil rights movement achieved?
options: Through decades of mass organising — NAACP legal work, grassroots campaigns, sit-ins, freedom rides — alongside leaders like King and Malcolm X.
Malcolm X and MLK were close allies who jointly led the March on Washington.
Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' speech ended segregation.
Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
